findings.title: Checkpoint messages and queue payloads lack the promised typed allowlist
findings.actual: An undeclared extensionState object containing a synthetic refresh token survives export verbatim. restore accepts an invalid thinkingLevel, user content=42, undeclared role and queued message role=42/content=null. No real credential was used.
findings.impact: Undeclared sensitive extension data can enter durable checkpoints, and malformed nested data is accepted into Agent state instead of rejecting before work.
findings.cause: Root/runtime/continuation key allowlists coexist with a recursive field-name denylist and role-string-only message checks; queue payload validation checks only truthiness and thinkingLevel is assigned without enum validation.
findings.suggestion: Implement one versioned, recursively typed checkpoint DTO with explicit extension data registration; validate all transcript/runtime/prepared/pending/queue locations plus enums before export/restore. Preserve valid SDK custom messages using trusted schemas, and reject undeclared necessary data rather than silently stripping it.

findings.title: Model identity is not revalidated between restore and actual resume dispatch
findings.actual: Changing the registered selected model baseUrl before restore is rejected, but making the identical change after successful restore permits a mock provider dispatch with the changed URL. restore itself has zero dispatches.
findings.impact: A restored run can use model/provider configuration that no longer matches its checkpoint binding; a later binding or checkpoint error would be too late to prevent that request.
findings.cause: restore stores a reference to the mutable registered Model; resumeRuntime checks config and tools but returns activePauseRuntime.model without verifying its recorded model binding.
findings.suggestion: Retain the immutable selected model binding; resolve/verify it at resume and immediately before each restored-flow provider dispatch, including after preparation hooks. Freeze or copy trusted descriptors as appropriate; never reconstruct secrets/headers from checkpoint data.

findings.title: Prepared request rejects a legitimate tool selected from pauseToolRegistry
findings.actual: A tool registered only in pauseToolRegistry is selected by prepareRequest. The prepared-request checkpoint exports successfully with root toolNames=[] and runtime toolNames=[registered_only], but restore throws Agent pause request continuation is invalid. The corrected no-pause control executes that tool exactly once.
findings.impact: The new documented registry option produces checkpoints that cannot be restored at a supported pause boundary even though the same run works without pause.
findings.cause: Request-stage validation requires every continuation tool name to occur in state.toolNames, despite resolvePauseTools correctly supporting state.tools plus pauseToolRegistry.
findings.suggestion: Validate continuation against the original effective runtime subset and trusted full registry rather than against only public state.tools. Keep exact signature/version verification and duplicate/unknown rejection.
